topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Characteristic and Duality
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics major)

sections.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
lecture_lines: A planar graph has no crossing edges.
Vertices and edges define bounded regions, or faces.
Don't forget the infinite face surrounding it.
animations: Visualize a simple graph with nodes and edges appearing on screen, using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg] as a template for node structure. Use color #FFFFFF for nodes and #FF00FF for edges.
Highlight the planar nature by showing no overlapping edges. Use a glow effect with color #FFFF00 on edges.

Decompose the graph into simple components to show it is planar. Move components apart using shift animation while maintaining the node style defined by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].

sections.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
lecture_lines: Euler's formula connects vertices, edges, and faces.
The formula is V minus E plus F equals 2.
It holds for every connected planar graph.
animations: Display the Euler formula: V - E + F = 2. Use color #00FFFF for the formula text.

Iteratively highlight vertices (V), edges (E), and faces (F) on a sample graph [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/graph.svg]. Use colors #FF0000 for V, #00FF00 for E, #0000FF for F.

Simulate adding a new vertex and edge on the graph [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/graph.svg] while showing the formula update. Highlight the formula with color #FFFF00 during update.

sections.title: The Concept of Graph Duality
lecture_lines: Construct the dual graph by placing nodes in faces.
Connect dual nodes if faces share an edge.
The dual graph acts like a structural mirror.
animations: Display the dual graph construction process by placing a vertex in each face. Use color #FFFFFF for dual nodes.
Connect dual vertices across edges of the original graph. Use color #FFA500 for dual edges.

Show the original graph fading out and the dual graph fading in, highlighting the topological transformation using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mirror.svg] to represent the duality. Use color #808080 for background transitions.

sections.title: Connecting Euler and Duality
lecture_lines: Dual graph properties relate to the original.
Vertices in one become faces in another.
Euler's formula reflects this duality symmetry.
animations: Show the original graph and its dual graph overlaid in different colors (#FF0000 and #0000FF), utilizing the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/map.svg] to represent the planar embedding.
Highlight the correspondence between V-F and F-V relationships. Use pulsing color #FFFF00 for connected parts within the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/node.svg] structures.

Demonstrate the transformation of E remains invariant between original and dual. Use a morphing animation effect with color #00FF00, integrated within the global [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/network.svg].

sections.title: Real-world Application
lecture_lines: VLSI circuits use planarity to prevent shorts.
Topology maps simplify complex pathfinding tasks.
Euler's formula remains a powerful geometric tool.
animations: Display a printed circuit board diagram. Use color #00FF00 for paths.
Show how graph duality optimizes the pathing on the circuit board. Highlight efficiency paths with color #FFFF00.
Summarize the application showing the graph abstraction over the real-world device. Overlay the graph in #FFFFFF over the circuit board image.
